The 12-minute script workflow that 10x'd a creator's views

🧵 Thread: How to automate viral scriptwriting in 12 minutes

---

The problem: Most creators spend 3+ hours writing scripts that get 200 views.

The algorithm buries you in the first 3 seconds because your structure doesn't match retention signals.

I analyzed 10,000 viral Reels/TikToks. The top 1% share 4 structural traits.

---

Framework 1: AIDA (Attention → Interest → Desire → Action)

Used for: YouTube intros, long-form retention.

The agent auto-applies this to your raw notes — no manual study needed.

---

Framework 2: PAS (Problem → Agitation → Solution)

Used for: LinkedIn, educational content.

Identifies audience pain, twists the knife, presents your method as the relief.

---

Framework 3: Hook-Value-CTA (Short-form optimized)

Used for: Reels, TikTok, Shorts (<60s).

Hook (0-3s) → Dense value (3-30s) → Frictionless CTA (last 3s).

Generates 5 hook types per script = built-in A/B testing.

---

Framework 4: StoryBrand (Narrative clarity)

Used for: YouTube descriptions, email sequences.

Character → Problem → Guide → Plan → CTA → Success/Failure.

Turns your content into a story the audience sees themselves in.

---

The game-changer: Auto-generated B-roll table.

Time | Voiceover | Visual | Text Overlay | SFX

Your editor drags & drops. Zero guesswork. Cuts editing time 50%.

Most creators skip this. That's why their retention curves flatline.

---

One raw input → 4 platform outputs:

📱 Instagram/TikTok: Dynamic, emojis, retention hooks
💼 LinkedIn: Narrative, authority, question CTA
🐦 Twitter/X: Thread format, viral mechanics
📺 YouTube: SEO, timestamps, chapters

Maximum distribution per unit effort.

---

Beta results (50 creators, 7 days):
• 47/50 saw ≥2x retention
• Avg production: 3h → 12min
• Avg views: 200 → 15,000
• Platform split: 40% Reels, 30% TikTok, 20% Shorts, 10% LinkedIn Video

The data doesn't lie. Structure beats effort.

---

The uncomfortable truth: Content calendars are traps. Dynamic systems win.
